speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To better understand your condition, can you tell me exactly how much bleeding you are experiencing and whether you have had any pelvic pain or urinary symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old woman. The patient presents with a 2-month history of intermittent postmenopausal bleeding. She denies any recent weight loss, fever, or changes in bladder or bowel habits. No previous history of similar symptoms. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications regularly.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Regarding your adnexal mass, have you noticed any associated pelvic pain, bloating, or changes in your appetite or bowel habits? Also, do you have any family history of ovarian or breast cancer?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Intermittent bleeding from the vagina. I also have No recent weight loss, No fever, No changes in bladder or bowel habits. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I must clarify that pyelonephritis (a kidney infection) does not cause postmenopausal bleeding or an adnexal mass; those findings suggest a gynecological issue. Given your age and the presence of a mass, I need to request imaging to evaluate the uterus and ovaries.

REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_Ultrasound
REQUEST TEST: Endometrial_Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic Ultrasound shows a thickened endometrial stripe and a left adnexal mass. Endometrial Biopsy reveals well-differentiated adenocarcinoma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Endometrial Adenocarcinoma with concurrent Ovarian Mass (likely metastatic spread or synchronous primary).

Given the biopsy results and the presence of an adnexal mass, I need to stage this disease. Do you have any history of breast cancer, and what is the result of your most recent CA-125 blood test?

REQUEST TEST: CA-125
REQUEST TEST: CT Abdomen and Pelvis
